items.headline: Simplifying agent access while keeping organizations in control: MCP servers, CLI, standardized usage tiers, and admin policies
items.summary: As AI agents transform how people work, we want to make it simple for developers to build agentic workflows while keeping organizations in control of their data in Google Workspace. We are making Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and the official Workspace CLI generally available alongside standardized usage tiers to simplify how developers build and scale agents, paired with a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls over AI agents. Simplifying and securing agent access with governed Workspace MCP servers and the Workspace CLI Developers now have two Google-managed ways to connect AI agents to Workspace without custom integration code: Workspace MCP serv
lines: Google is making Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and the official Workspace CLI generally available, along with standardized usage tiers for developers building agents.
Google also introduced a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls over AI agents.
Developers can connect AI agents to Workspace without custom integration code, while organizations keep control of their data.

items.headline: New study enhancements for Flashcards in Gemini Notebook
items.summary: We introduced three updates to flashcards in Gemini Notebook to help users better retain information, measure recall speed, and maintain consistent review routines. Images: Flashcards now automatically incorporate relevant images directly from uploaded source materials, providing visual context alongside text prompts to aid comprehension. Built-in stopwatch: Users can enable a stopwatch while reviewing flashcards to track time during the session, making it easier to simulate timed exam conditions. Mobile study reminders: Using the Gemini Notebook mobile app, users can schedule notifications reminding them to review previously generated flashcards, supporting structured study cadences. These
lines: Google added three updates to flashcards in Gemini Notebook to help users retain information, measure recall speed, and keep consistent review routines.
Flashcards now automatically include relevant images from uploaded source materials, and users can turn on a stopwatch during review.
Users of the Gemini Notebook mobile app can schedule reminders to review previously generated flashcards.

items.headline: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available: Unified observability across every layer of your stack
items.summary: Observability is critical for running software in production. It helps teams understand whether a service is healthy, why a request slowed down, and what changed before an incident began. Answering those questions draws on more than one signal. Metrics show that behavior has changed, logs record what happened, and traces show where along a request’s path it happened. These signals are most useful when you can move from one to the next without losing context. As a stack grows to span clusters, databases, and agents, a unified view across every layer allows a team to keep pace with the system it operates. DigitalOcean Insights gives you a unified observability stack built into the DigitalOcean
lines: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available as a unified observability stack built into DigitalOcean.
The product brings together metrics, logs, and traces so users can move between signals without losing context.
It is aimed at stacks that span clusters, databases, and agents.

items.headline: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Security Advisory: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products Palo Alto Networks is aware of the two Critical Severity vulnerabilities in NGINX: CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007. CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free vulnerability in NGINX HTTP/2 proxy handling where active connections fail to clear their reusable state. When worker connection slots run low, NGINX can prematurely close and free memory for connections still actively proxying requests to upstream servers. lines: Palo Alto Networks published an advisory on two Critical severity NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, and their impact on its products.
CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free flaw in NGINX HTTP/2 proxy handling that can let an unauthenticated remote attacker crash worker processes or execute arbitrary code.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Iran-aligned espionage group Volant Manticore, previously undocumented, has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.
